name: agent_teams_add_member
description: Add a member to the team roster. Planning and idle roster rows do not call a model. After approval, the member session starts with its first ready task or explicit message and remains durable for later work.

name.description: Unique member name inside the team.

role.description: Role of the member (e.g. researcher, engineer, reviewer).

provider.description: Optional LLM provider route. Use only when the user explicitly requests a different provider; requires model. Omit to use the configured member route (memberLlmProvider/memberModel) or the captain's current route.

model.description: Optional model override (used verbatim, including any "/" in the id). Omit for the configured memberModel default (paired with memberLlmProvider when set) or the captain's current model.

reasoning_effort.description: Optional reasoning effort override: one of the target model's supported effort ids, or "default" to force its default. When omitted, the captain's effort is inherited only for the same provider/model; a changed route uses the target default.

executionPrompt.description: Optional member-specific execution prompt. It remains editable while staged.

tool_policy.description: Optional id of a tool policy declared by the deployment owner (config toolPolicies). It restricts which global tools this member sees and may invoke: a policy allow-list also keeps the four coordination tools, and captain-only tools can never be reopened. Omit for the unchanged default tool set.

name: agent_teams_amend_task
description: Captain-only controlled contract amendment for one non-terminal quality task: replace a wrong objective/acceptance/verify/inScope/outOfScope when the original contract makes honest completion impossible (for example a verify command that cannot pass, or an inScope that forbids the file the objective names). The amendment is appended to the task's revisions ledger with previous values and the reason, and is rejected once a review/requirements task has passed judgment on this task. Members cannot amend contracts; the implementer re-reads the amended contract before its next quality gate. Lists are full replacements, not deltas.

task_id.description: Task whose contract is being amended.

reason.description: Why the current contract is wrong; recorded in the revisions ledger.

acceptance.description: Replacement acceptance criteria (full list, not a delta).

verify.description: Replacement verification commands (full list, not a delta).

name: agent_teams_approve
description: Approve and start a staged team plan. Call this only in response to an explicit user approval in a new user turn; never call it during the turn that created or edited the plan. The Web Approve & Run button uses the same runtime directly.

name: agent_teams_claim_task
description: Members claim their own ready task or read their existing attempt_id. Captains must use reassign_task to assign and wake a member; claim_task does not dispatch work. A member cannot own a second unfinished task. The returned attempt_id is required for updates and becomes stale after retry/reassignment.

assignee.description: Deprecated: claim_task only supports a member claiming its own task. Captains must use reassign_task.

name: agent_teams_create
description: Create a team. Use approval=required for a two-phase plan: members and tasks remain unspawned/unclaimed until the user reviews the Web plan and explicitly approves it. Optional profiles expand their configured roster; seed profiles also expand template tasks, while captain profiles leave the graph for the Captain to design. approval=automatic preserves the legacy immediate-execution path.

name.description: Name for the new team (used as its stable id).

description.description: Team purpose / the goal the team will work on.

plan.description: Optional complete ordinary-work roster and DAG in one atomic call, instead of separate add_member/create_task rounds. Mutually exclusive with profile. For quality gates use create_task with the explicit quality contract.

tool_policy.description: Optional owner-declared tool-policy id for this member.

id.description: Local reference used by dependencies in this plan; the result maps it to a durable task id.

approval.description: required stages the plan for explicit user review; automatic starts immediately. Defaults to automatic for API compatibility.

name: agent_teams_create_task
description: Create a task in your team's task list. Use kind=work (default) for research, repository audits and general tasks. kind=review is only a quality gate for an existing implementation/repair task via reviewedTaskId. Every call must include a non-empty subject, including verification and review tasks. Tasks can depend on other tasks (dependencies): a task is only claimable once every dependency is completed. Optionally assign it to a member, who still claims it before working.

subject.description: Required non-empty title for this task. Never omit it, including for verification or review tasks.

description.description: What needs to be done, in detail.

dependencies.description: Task ids this task depends on (must be completed before this task can be claimed).

assignee.description: Member name when an owner is specified. Omission puts this task in the shared pool; roles, subjects and descriptions do not assign an owner.

kind.description: Explicit task kind. Omission means work with no quality gates, even if the subject says implementation/review. Quality kinds require a contract. An implementation may be planned before requirements passes when its dependency chain includes that requirements task.

objective.description: Required non-empty objective for quality kinds.

inScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task may change.

outOfScope.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths this task must not change.

acceptance.description: Acceptance criteria. Required for quality kinds.

reviewedTaskId.description: Existing AgentTeams implementation/repair task id. Required for kind=review; an external repository audit is kind=work.

sourceFindingIds.description: Finding ids this repair must close.

coverageOf.description: User-constraint / goal items this task covers.

resume.description: If true, clear halted in the same lock before creating the task.

name: agent_teams_delete
description: End and archive your team: interrupts members and moves the current tasks and mailboxes out of active state for later inspection. Use when the work is done or explicitly abandoned. A same-name archive replaces its previous generation.

name: agent_teams_edit_plan
description: Atomically revise an AgentTeams plan. While staged, edit tasks and roster without starting work. While running, only update_task is allowed, and only for pending tasks with no prior attempt: correct dependencies, assignees or descriptions before they start; newly ready work is scheduled after commit. Never edit active/finished attempts. Submit dependent edits in order. Never modify .agent-teams files directly.

operations.description: One atomic, ordered batch. Running teams allow only update_task for never-started pending tasks. If any operation is invalid, none of the edits are saved.

member_name.description: Member name for update_member or remove_member.

task_id.description: Task id for update_task or remove_task.

subject.description: Required for add_task; optional replacement for update_task.

assignee.description: Optional task assignee; an empty string moves it to the shared pool.

dependencies.description: Complete replacement dependency list for a task.

provider.description: Optional member provider; defaults to the current staged route.

model.description: Optional member model; defaults to the current staged route.

tool_policy.description: Optional owner-declared tool-policy id for this member; an empty string clears it back to the unchanged default tool set.

name: agent_teams_reassign_task
description: Atomically retry, reassign, or let the captain take over one ready unfinished/failed task. The old attempt is revoked before its member is interrupted, so late updates cannot overwrite the new owner. Use assignee="captain" only when you will finish that task in this turn; a captain can own only one unfinished takeover at a time, and an unfinished takeover returns to the member pool when the captain becomes idle.

assignee.description: Active member name, or "captain" for captain takeover.

reason.description: Why the task is being retried or reassigned.

name: agent_teams_remove_member
description: Remove a member safely: revoke its current attempts, return all unfinished owned tasks to the shared pending pool, interrupt its live turn, and mark it removed.

name.description: Name of the member to remove.

name: agent_teams_resume
description: Explicitly resume a halted team. Requires a non-empty reason. Does not recreate cancelled tasks; only still-pending work is scheduled.

reason.description: Why the team is being resumed.

name: agent_teams_send_message
description: Send coordination or current-task guidance directly to the captain or a teammate. A running recipient receives it at the next model step; an idle recipient wakes. Messages are durably retained until read. Use task creation/reassignment for a new unit of work, not repeated status nudges.

source_task_id.description: Sender task, NOT the recipient task. Members include it with source_attempt_id. Captains sending guidance normally omit both source fields.

source_attempt_id.description: Sender execution capability paired with source_task_id. Stale reports are rejected. Omit for ordinary captain guidance.

from.description: Sender (defaults to the caller: the captain, or the calling member).

name: agent_teams_status
description: Team snapshot: members with live activity and tasks with status/assignee/dependencies/output. Captains also see every team mailbox; members see only their own inbox. Use after mailbox progress deliveries or for an explicit status request. After dispatch, end your turn while members work; do not repeatedly poll.

name: agent_teams_update_task
description: Update a task status/output. Members must supply the current attempt_id returned by claim_task; stale attempts are rejected after takeover/reassignment. Terminal results are immutable, but owners and the captain can append acceptanceResults/commandsRun/evidence_note as attributed supplemental evidence, without reclaiming or changing the verdict. A captain must use reassign_task(assignee="captain") before updating active member-owned work.

attempt_id.description: Members must explicitly include the current attempt_id from their assignment/claim in EVERY update, including failed reviews with findings. If omitted, retry with the same current id; omission does not revoke the attempt.

output.description: Original result summary; immutable after completion/failure.

evidence_note.description: Append-only supplementary observation on a terminal task. Does not reopen work or change the original result.

verdict.description: Required for completing requirements/review. needs_revision and reject must fail the task.

findings.description: Structured review findings. Required when verdict is needs_revision or reject; each item needs id, severity, problem, and requiredFix.

changedPaths.description: Workspace-relative POSIX paths changed by this implementation/repair.

acceptanceResults.description: Acceptance evidence in contract order: {criterion, status:"passed"|"failed", evidence?}. Supply one item per acceptance criterion.

commandsRun.description: Verification evidence in contract order: {command, status:"passed"|"failed", exitCode?, evidence?}. Supply one item per verify command.

name: ask_user_question
description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding. An answer item with empty selected and no custom means the user skipped that question: continue without it, do not ask it again, and do not treat the skip as permission.

questions.description: Questions to ask the user before continuing.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

question.description: The specific question to ask the user.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

name: bash
description:
Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Git for Windows (MSYS) converts path-looking arguments when invoking native Windows programs: ipconfig /all and cmd /c may break; use ipconfig //all or cmd //c, or a per-command MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL prefix. Exclusions are prefixes: excluding /c also excludes /c/... paths, so use native drive-letter paths for those arguments; do not disable conversion globally. Verify the expected effect as well as the exit code. Output is decoded as UTF-8; native Windows programs may emit OEM/ANSI bytes (for example CP936/GBK) and display garbled text. Use a program UTF-8 option or explicit known-encoding conversion before capture; locale variables alone do not fix native output, and mixed streams cannot safely be guessed or decoded globally as GBK. On Windows, while Experimental native execution / fail-closed (experimentalNative, default ON) is enabled, read-only/workspace-write or unresolved policy is refused before this Git Bash command starts because verified confinement is unavailable. Only an explicitly resolved danger-full-access policy can execute this route. The user can turn off that switch in Settings > Plugins > dsh-gitbash-shell to restore explicitly UNCONFINED legacy Bash, or select danger-full-access in the session access-mode control. Do not switch tools or permissions automatically to bypass a refusal; official file-tool write/edit policy remains separate.
[gitbash tool routing]
Prefer this bash tool for shell syntax, scripts, pipelines, redirection, globbing and POSIX utilities — it is this host's shell.
Fix failed bash syntax in bash; no PowerShell tool is offered here. Do not invent a hidden tool or embed another interpreter as a workaround.
Use gitbash_native before execution when a Windows .exe needs exact literal argv such as /all or /c without MSYS conversion, or independently declared stdout/stderr encodings. Supply an absolute executable, mark each argument literal or path, and select only a known encoding (raw for unknown/mixed bytes). It does not implement shell pipelines, expansion or .cmd/.bat wrappers; only resolved danger-full-access can execute it.
Use gitbash_to_native_path only for a complete caller-declared MSYS filesystem path that a native Node fs/path API needs, especially a runtime-built value. Read native_path from the result. Never convert routes, search strings or shell/program source. Already-native or cwd-relative Node paths need no conversion; ordinary tool path fields already use their own translation. Conversion grants no access.
Choose the execution route before running. A policy/access denial is a stop condition: never switch tools, shells or permissions to bypass it. A decoding/display failure does not mean the command failed to run; preserve its exit facts and never blindly repeat a side-effecting command. Do not guess unknown or mixed encodings.
This bash is Git for Windows (MSYS): paths use drive roots (/c/Users/...), and ~, /tmp, /dev/null and /usr/... resolve exactly as Git Bash resolves them.
[/gitbash tool routing]

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

name: create_goal
description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

name: create_worktree
description: Create a new Git branch and worktree from a local commit, branch, or tag, then change this session's working directory to it. Uncommitted files stay in the source checkout. Existing names fail. Use working_directory with cd to leave; the checkout and branch remain.

name.description: New branch name, also used as the checkout directory: a few lowercase words joined by hyphens that describe the task, such as fix-login-retry. Omit to generate a unique name.

from.description: Local commit, branch, or tag to start from. Defaults to HEAD; no fetch is performed.

name: edit
description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `old_string` and `new_string` in the arguments.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

name: get_goal
description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

name: gitbash_native
description: Choose this tool BEFORE execution for a Windows-native .exe that needs exact literal argv (for example /all or /c without MSYS conversion) or explicitly known independent stdout/stderr encodings. Use an offered shell tool instead for pipelines, redirection, globbing, shell expansion or POSIX scripts; this is direct typed argv through the host managed executor, not shell source. Supply an absolute executable, mark literal arguments unchanged and path arguments explicitly; do not put a whole shell command into argv. Prefer a producer UTF-8 option; declare gbk/utf16le only when known, raw for unknown or mixed bytes. In PTC call this offered SDK binding from inside run_code, not as a direct model tool call. Only actual danger-full-access standing policy is supported; missing/restricted policy is rejected before execution. A policy/access denial is a stop condition, never permission for another-tool retry. Decoding/storage failure preserves producer exit: never blindly repeat side effects. No user env, implicit scripts, .cmd/.bat wrappers, path guessing or encoding auto-detection. Known interpreters require explicit entrypoint:interpreter; common CRT/Node argv is supported, arbitrary interpreter quoting is not guaranteed.

description.description: Short description of the intended native operation.

executable.description: Absolute native .exe path. MSYS paths translate only in kind:path values. Bare commands, scripts, .cmd and .bat are unsupported.

argv.description: Each literal is passed unchanged (including /all, /c, quotes and empty strings); each path must be absolute and is explicitly translated to native Windows spelling. No shell expansion.

cwd.description: Absolute typed working directory; omitted means the agent workspace.

entrypoint.description: Default native. Known interpreters require explicit interpreter. Their own command language/quoting is not made safe by direct argv; no automatic script wrapper.

timeoutMs.description: Foreground wait deadline, default 120000ms, capped at 600000ms; expiry promotes the managed process to a job. Not accepted with run_in_background.

run_in_background.description: Use existing managed Jobs; collect with job_output, stop with job_kill. No tool deadline. Requires an attached job controller.

stdoutEncoding.description: Known producer stdout encoding, default utf8. raw preserves unknown/mixed bytes without claiming reliable text. No auto detection.

stderrEncoding.description: Known producer stderr encoding, independently selected; default utf8.

errors.description: Default replace; strict records decoding failures separately from actual command exit. Never rerun a side-effecting command merely because output decoding failed.

name: gitbash_to_native_path
description: Explicitly convert one complete caller-declared path value from the MSYS/Git Bash dialect (/c/-style drive roots, ~, $HOME-style variables, /tmp, /dev/null, Git installation mounts) to its native Windows form and return { native_path }. Call this ONLY when the full value is already known to be a single filesystem path — the tool never inspects surrounding data and never guesses. Pure string conversion through the plugin's shared mount table: no filesystem I/O, no existence check, no permission grant; your runtime policy still governs the converted path. Values that are already Windows-native (drive-letter or UNC) or cwd-relative are returned unchanged, by design. A POSIX-looking value that no mount maps — or whose needed mount fact is unavailable — is REJECTED with an explicit error instead of a misleading passthrough. Independent of the automatic dialect switches; the parameter is named msys_path so the automatic path-field rewrite leaves it untouched. Use it for runtime-built MSYS paths before direct native Node fs/path I/O: await the result and pass result.native_path, never the original MSYS string. Already-native/cwd-relative Node values or ordinary translated tool path fields need no conversion. Never pass routes, search strings, shell commands or program source. In PTC invoke this offered SDK binding from inside run_code. A file policy/access denial is a stop condition, not a reason to convert the spelling and retry through Node or another tool.

msys_path.description: The complete value to convert, as one single MSYS/Git Bash path (drive root /c/, ~, $HOME-style variable, /tmp, /dev/null or a Git install mount). Pass the FULL value only; the tool performs no I/O and no permission grant.

name: github
description: Call the GitHub REST API. The credential stays inside the plugin — it is never returned, and every result is redacted. Write methods require confirm: true.

path.description: API path after https://api.github.com/, e.g. repos/o/r/issues.

name: glob
description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

name: grep
description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

name: hindsight_capture_initiative
description:
Record a new feature or initiative as a tracked knowledge page, so future sessions know it exists and can build on it — and keep that page tracking the plan as it moves.

WHEN TO CALL:
- Starting one: right after the user approves a plan or finishes brainstorming a new feature/capability and you are about to start implementing — BEFORE you write any code. Leave relates_to_page_id empty.
- Plan changed: call it AGAIN — mid-implementation is fine and expected — whenever the goal, scope, or rationale of an initiative you already captured materially changes (an approach is dropped, scope grows or shrinks, the why is rewritten). Pass relates_to_page_id = that initiative's page id so the change lands on the existing page. Never mint a second page for the same initiative.

WHEN TO SKIP: bug fixes, small tweaks, refactors, chores, and trivial course-corrections that leave the goal intact are not initiatives — skip them.

- title: short, specific name (e.g. 'Newsletter refinement chat'). On a recapture, reuse the initiative's existing title.
- summary: 2-3 sentences on what you're building and why — the CURRENT intent, not the originally approved plan (on a recapture, say what changed and why).
- relates_to_page_id: leave empty for a new initiative. Set it to an existing initiative's page id — from hindsight_list_knowledge_pages, or the id this tool returned earlier — to record a plan change or an enhancement to it.

Returns the page id. The page is generated for you — you never format one yourself.

name: hindsight_diagnose
description: Report safe Hindsight runtime diagnostics for this coding-agent session: resolved bank, workspace, harness, config location, API endpoint, and non-secret environment overrides. Use this when memory, hooks, MCP tools, or configuration appear not to work. Tokens and other secret values are never returned.

name: hindsight_ingest_document
description: Save an external document or a block of durable notes/findings into this repository's memory so it informs future recall and pages. Use for design notes, research, or reference material you want remembered — not for the conversation you're already in (that's captured automatically at session end). This is ALSO the correction mechanism: when you verify that a retrieved memory is wrong or outdated, ingest a document titled 'Correction: <topic>' stating what memory claimed, what is actually true, and the evidence — the newer fact supersedes the stale one in future retrieval.

name: hindsight_list_knowledge_pages
description: List this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages — curated, continuously-updated summaries of the project's durable knowledge (architecture, components, conventions, key decisions, and in-flight initiatives). Returns each page's id, title, and a one-line description of what it covers. Call this at the start of any non-trivial task, and again periodically in long sessions, to see what the project already knows before you read code or ask the user. The list changes as work is captured, so re-check it occasionally.

name: hindsight_read_knowledge_page
description: Read the full content of one knowledge page by its id (from hindsight_list_knowledge_pages). Call this whenever a listed page is relevant to what you're about to do — e.g. read Conventions before writing new code, Component map before changing a subsystem, or an initiative's page before continuing that feature. A page may contain [[page:<id>]] links to related pages; follow one by calling this tool again with that id. Prefer reading a page over re-deriving the same understanding from source.

name: hindsight_reflect
description: Deep memory reasoning: an agentic synthesis over this repository's FULL memory (git decisions, past sessions, ingested knowledge) that answers WHY questions — the past decision and exact rule/values that explain a behavior, bug, or convention. Slower than hindsight_search_knowledge_pages (several seconds): reach for it when pages are too shallow and you need the root cause or the decided literals. When the answer informs your reply, credit it visibly with a blockquote header: "> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory** — <summary>".

query.description: the question to reason over memory about

name: hindsight_search_knowledge_pages
description: Search this repository's Hindsight knowledge pages for content relevant to a query — hybrid full-text + semantic search, server-side. Call this when the user's question may be answered by the project's accumulated knowledge (architecture, conventions, decisions, initiatives) rather than by reading code. Returns ranked pages with a relevance snippet; read a full page with hindsight_read_knowledge_page. Crediting is mandatory, not a judgement call: if anything these results contribute reaches your reply — quoted, paraphrased, or merely confirming what you were going to say — open that part with "> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory (<page>)** — <the specific facts you drew on>". Rewriting a snippet in your own words does not make it yours. If none of them bear on the turn, ignore them silently — an unhelpful search needs no mention. These are past records: check a claim that something was fixed or works against the code before relying on it.

name: hindsight_sync_status
description: Report whether this repo's memory bank is in sync: gitlog seed present, how much recent history has been deepened with full diffs, conversations ingested, knowledge pages created, and extractions still running. `synced: true` means the seeded memory is fully queryable. Ingestion is automatic and background — if not synced, it is in progress; nothing to run.

name: interrupt_agent
description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local subagent's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent.description: The name of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

name: job_kill
description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

name: job_list
description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

name: job_output
description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

name: kifu_card
description: 生成与线上注入**同一份**记忆卡（跑十道闸）：给定文本，返回卡片正文、token 数、逐条 claim 与闸门结论。

text.description: 要查的文本（用户这句话 / 报错原文 / 主题词）。空串会被拒。

limit.description: 返回条数上限（会被夹紧到 1–50）。

scope.description: 作用域键（w:…）。不传 = 不限域；传了就只返回该域可见内容（A5 同语义）。

name: kifu_get
description: 按 id 取一条记录（kinds: episodes/topics/claims/links/threads/joseki/adjudications）。只读。

id.description: 记录 id（如 c-xxxxxxxx / ep-xxxxxxxx / t:…）。

name: kifu_recent_failures
description: 最近的失败原文（按 occurredAt 倒序，带 ep+seq 出处）：用来"先取已付过代价的失败"。只读、零模型。

limit.description: 返回条数上限（会被夹紧到 1–50）。

scope.description: 作用域键（w:…）。不传 = 不限域；传了就只返回该域可见内容（A5 同语义）。

name: kifu_search
description: 按文本找相关记忆（轻量命中列表：棋谱 + seq + 种类 + 权重 + 命中理由）。只读、零模型。

text.description: 要查的文本（用户这句话 / 报错原文 / 主题词）。空串会被拒。

limit.description: 返回条数上限（会被夹紧到 1–50）。

scope.description: 作用域键（w:…）。不传 = 不限域；传了就只返回该域可见内容（A5 同语义）。

name: kifu_stats

name: kifu_view
description: 以某个节点为中心的**邻域视图**（18×18 ≈ 324 节点）：返回中心 + 相连节点/边，边界边进 frontier；不够时顺着 frontier 再调一次。只读、零模型。

id.description: 中心节点 id（如 ep-xxxxxxxx / c-xxxxxxxx / lib:docs/调研）。

scope.description: 作用域键（w:…）。不传 = 不限域；传了就只返回该域可见内容（A5 同语义）。

name: list_agents
description: List your entire subagent tree: the root agent and all reachable continuable descendants, including yourself. Rows carry names, descriptions, and status. A descendant's name is its path from the root, such as reviewer/checker. You can message any other agent in the subagent tree. running means it is working; inactive means no turn is executing; it does not indicate task completion, success, or failure. corrupt, unsupported, or unavailable means this row's own descendants could not be read; the row itself is still a member you can message. While you remain active, you will be notified when a direct child finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

name: list_subagent_models
description: Inspect the routes available for explicit subagent model selection. No arguments: authorized providers. `provider`: that provider's authorized models. `provider` + `model`: that model and its reasoning efforts. Query when choosing an explicit child route or reasoning effort. Omit optional fields rather than sending empty strings.

name: load_workspace_dependencies
description: Get absolute paths to bundled Python and library directories, plus bundled Python distribution versions. Node.js and pnpm paths are included when the payload provides them. Python includes numpy, pandas, python-docx, python-pptx, openpyxl, Pillow, lxml, and XlsxWriter. Use these libraries for Office files unless the user or workspace instructions select another environment. When Node.js and pnpm paths are returned, run pnpm with that Node executable and pnpm script path. This does not change PATH or package-manager settings.

name: present
description: Declare existing files as final deliverables for the user. Hosts may show presented files only after your turn ends, so call it once the files are final. If the user needs to review files earlier, such as before a tool call that waits for their answer, link them in your message instead. Use it when the user needs a separate file, especially Office documents, spreadsheets, and slide decks; prefer your final response when that suffices. The user opens the current files; their contents are not copied.

files.description: Usually the 1-2 most important deliverables; at most 4 per call.

path.description: Path of an existing regular file. Relative paths use the Session working directory.

name: pwsh
description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

name: read
description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

name: read_image
description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Large images are downscaled automatically; do not install image libraries or create thumbnails to inspect an image.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

name: repo_here
description: Report the GitHub repository of the current working directory (owner/name, default branch, visibility). Read-only.

name: schedule_create
description: Create a scheduled task. At each occurrence of rrule, prompt is delivered to the target session as a scheduled message from the user. The result includes the task id and the next occurrence as scheduledAt in UTC and scheduledAtLocal in the zone of rrule. After downtime, only the latest missed occurrence is delivered. Delivery can repeat after a crash.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes.

rrule.description: Supported RFC 5545 subset: one DTSTART line, a newline, and one RRULE line. DTSTART ends in Z for UTC or carries TZID with an IANA time zone; a fixed offset such as UTC+5 is Etc/GMT-5, with the sign reversed. DTSTART must name an existing local time. A TZID rule keeps local clock time across daylight-saving changes; generated nonexistent local times are skipped, and repeated ones occur once, at the earlier instant. DTSTART may be in the past; delivery starts with the first occurrence after creation. A one-time delivery is RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1. No SECONDLY; BYSECOND takes one value. COUNT is at most 1000; use UNTIL for longer rules. MINUTELY and HOURLY accept no BY parts, so select clock times with DAILY or WEEKLY plus BYHOUR and BYMINUTE. BYMONTHDAY and ordinal BYDAY require MONTHLY or YEARLY; BYYEARDAY and BYWEEKNO require YEARLY. Ordinal BYDAY cannot combine with BYWEEKNO. Each FREQ period allows at most 10080 candidates before BYSETPOS, which accepts at most 31 values. UNTIL is a UTC instant ending in Z. Example: "DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Singapore:20260901T080000\nRRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR;BYSETPOS=-1"

target.description: this_session delivers to this session; new_once delivers to the same new session every time, opened at the first delivery; new opens a different new session for every delivery. New sessions use this session's working directory and preset. With this_session or new_once, a delivery waits until the previous one finishes, and only the latest occurrence that passed meanwhile is delivered. Use this_session for reminders and for follow-ups to this conversation; use new_once or new for independent work, such as a recurring report, and whenever the user asks for a new conversation.

name: schedule_edit
description: Update, pause, resume, or delete one scheduled task by id. Deleting does not retract queued messages.

action.description: update applies the provided fields, at least one; delete removes the task.

title.description: Task name of at most 120 characters in the user's language: action plus object. Omit timing, status, ids, and bracketed suffixes.

prompt.description: New instruction delivered at each occurrence.

rrule.description: New recurrence in the schedule_create rrule format.

target.description: Omit to retain the destination and its creation settings. Providing target replaces them; new_once reserves a different Session. New targets capture this Session's working directory and preset. Choices are the same as schedule_create.

active.description: false pauses the task; true resumes only if its timing has a future occurrence. Otherwise provide a new rrule.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: updatedAt from the latest result that returned this task; if the task changed after that result, the result is schedule_conflict and nothing changes.

name: schedule_list
description: List scheduled tasks, including tasks created from other sessions. Active tasks come first, ordered by scheduledAt.

active.description: true for active tasks only; false for paused and ended tasks only; omitted for all tasks.

limit.description: Page size from 1 to 500; defaults to 100.

offset.description: Number of tasks to skip; defaults to 0.

name: schedule_view
description: View one scheduled task by id.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation.

agent.description: The name of another agent in your subagent tree, as shown by list_agents.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

name: sidebar_open
description: Open a local file, a local folder, or an HTTP(S) page in the sidebar of the calling conversation. A file opens in the sidebar editor (per-path dedupe: an already-open file is focused); a folder opens a file window whose tree is rooted at that folder; a URL opens in the sidebar browser (sandboxed iframe). The panel auto-expands for content opens and the tab title defaults to the file/folder name or the URL hostname. The path may be absolute or relative to the session working directory. The open lands in the CALLING session's sidebar: while that session's sidebar view is not connected (e.g. the session is not the active one), the open is queued and delivered when the session sidebar is next shown — the result reports `delivered` so you know whether it is visible right now. The side card setting "model opens files/folders/pages in the sidebar" must be on, and the target tab type must be enabled in that session's settings.

target.description: Absolute or session-cwd-relative local path, or an http:// / https:// URL.

title.description: Optional tab title (defaults to the file/folder name or the URL hostname).

name: skill
description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

name: subagent
description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its name. If you are still online when it finishes, the runtime automatically delivers its completion notice. The notice includes the final answer unless the child sent you a message just before finishing. Use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes. Omit `provider`, `model`, and `reasoning_effort` to use child defaults, falling back to compatible parent values.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display. Use the language of the user's current request.

name.description: Optional short name for the subagent, unique among the subagents you create: lower-case letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters; lead is reserved for the root agent. Omitted names default to agent-1, agent-2, and so on.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

model.description: Model id within that provider; requires `provider`.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort id; requires `provider` and `model`. Omit to use the selected model's default, even when it matches the parent or configured route.

name: subagent_fork
description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its name. If you are still online when it finishes, the runtime automatically delivers its completion notice. The notice includes the final answer unless the child sent you a message just before finishing. Use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display. Use the language of the user's current request.

name.description: Optional short name for the subagent, unique among the subagents you create: lower-case letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter, at most 32 characters; lead is reserved for the root agent. Omitted names default to agent-1, agent-2, and so on.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

name: team_task_create
description: Create one unowned pending task on the shared Team task board.

description.description: Complete task details and acceptance criteria.

blocked_by.description: Task ids that must complete first.

write_scopes.description: Advisory workspace-relative file or directory prefixes this task expects to modify.

name: team_task_get
description: Read the complete latest value of one shared task before changing or executing it.

name: team_task_list
description: List shared tasks, including readiness, owner, revision, blockers, and write-scope warnings.

owner.description: Optional owner agent name filter; cannot be combined with unowned.

unowned.description: Filter tasks by whether they have no owner; cannot be combined with owner.

limit.description: Number of rows, 1 through 100. Defaults to 50.

name: team_task_update
description: Compare-and-set a shared task action using the latest revision from team_task_get or team_task_list.

expected_revision.description: Current task revision used as the CAS precondition.

write_scopes.description: Replacement advisory write scopes for edit.

owner.description: Agent name of the root or any continuable descendant for root-only reassign; omit to unassign.

name: todo_write
description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

name: unlag_refresh
description: 按一下刷新按钮；关闭时说明原因

requestId.description: 这次刷新的名字；同样的名字只刷新一次

name: update_goal
description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

name: wait_agent
description: Wait for input at your next step, including agent messages, completion notifications, and user steering. Returns immediately if new input is pending. `timedOut: false` means new input is pending. Pending input is delivered to the model after code execution finishes.

timeout_ms.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, from 10000 through 3600000. Defaults to 30000.

name: watch_ack
description: Mark an issue/PR as handled: adds the ack label (主理鱼:已处理 by default on GitHub, 主理鱼-已处理 on Gitee) and advances the local watermark, so the same item will never wake this session again — even after a restart or on another machine.

repo.description: owner/name; defaults to the only watched repo

number.description: issue or PR number（Gitee 的编号是字符串，如 IKSQJH）

numbers.description: 逗号分隔的多个编号，如 "12,13,14"（number 与 numbers 至少填一个）

label.description: ack label, default 主理鱼:已处理 on GitHub / 主理鱼-已处理 on Gitee

note.description: 可选：一句话记下这条最后怎么处理的（如「已修，见 #57」「不修，上游已修」）。下次这条再被叫醒时会带回来，省得会话重新判一遍。

comment.description: 把 note 作为评论回写到原 issue/PR（默认 false）。必须同时给 note；这是显式写操作。

kind.description: Gitee 评论回写时的条目类型：'issue'（默认）或 'pull'；GitHub 不需要。

name: watch_doctor
description: Self-check the watchers: gh login, repo access, ack label existence, isolation workdir. Prints a checklist. It does not change any watcher config, but it does write one temporary probe file inside the isolation workdir (and deletes it immediately) to prove the directory is writable.

repo.description: only check this owner/name; default = every watcher

name: watch_start
description: Watch a repository and wake THIS session when its issues or pull requests change. Works with GitHub (owner/name) and Gitee (prefix with gitee:, e.g. gitee:owner/name; a gitee.com URL also works). Pass several repos in one call separated by spaces or commas to create several watchers at once. Idempotent per (repo, session). Default interval 60 s, minimum 30 s.

repo.description: owner/name (GitHub) 或 gitee:owner/name（Gitee）；多个用空格或逗号分隔。Omit to infer from the current working directory.

intervalSec.description: Polling interval in seconds, clamped to 30-3600, default 60.

labels.description: Only handle items carrying one of these labels (whitelist).

ignoreLabels.description: Skip items carrying any of these labels.

onlyAssigned.description: Only handle items assigned to someone (or to `assignee`).

allowAuthors.description: 只要这些人提的（GitHub 登录名，可带 @）。空 = 谁都算。用来挡掉别人随手提的 issue。

observe.description: Observe only: record what WOULD be woken, never wake.

isolated.description: Run each wake in a throwaway git worktree.

workdir.description: Repository used for isolation worktrees (absolute path).

activeHours.description: Wake only inside this window, e.g. "09:00-23:00" (supports overnight).

resume.description: Only when the watcher is paused: resume it (default true). Pass false to change config while keeping it paused.

batchLimit.description: Max items listed per wake (1-20, default 5).

maxWakesPerHour.description: Max wakes per hour per watcher (1-60, default 6).

sessionMaxWakes.description: Max wakes per hour for the whole session, summed across watchers (1-60, default 12).

isolateKeepDays.description: With isolated: remove isolation worktrees older than this many days (1-30, default 3).

maxIsolated.description: With isolated: keep at most this many worktrees, oldest removed first (1-50, default 5).

goal.description: Optional per-watcher goal appended to the wake message.

ackLabel.description: Label used as the handled marker (default 主理鱼:已处理 on GitHub / 主理鱼-已处理 on Gitee). Two sessions watching the same repo share it unless each sets its own.

priority.description: Priority switches; only explicitly supplied keys are changed. Boolean keys: reopened, comments, labels, unassigned, stale. Defaults: reopened/comments/labels=true; unassigned/stale=false. additionalProperties are unrestricted.

name: watch_status
description: Report active watchers: schedule, why one is paused, unanswered wakes, and how much of the session wake budget is used. Use format=json for machine-readable output. Read-only.

name: watch_stop
description: Stop watching a repository for the current session. By default this pauses it and keeps its state; pass delete:true to remove it and leave a tombstone.

delete.description: Delete the watcher and persist a tombstone instead of only pausing it (default false).

name: watch_trace
description: Explain what happened to one issue/PR: whether it was filtered (and why), absorbed by the cooldown, already reported, or never seen. Read-only — changes nothing. Use it when the customer asks "why did this not wake me".

repo.description: owner/name; defaults to the only watched repo

number.description: issue or PR number to trace

name: web_fetch
description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

name: web_search
description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–10 search queries; their results are merged.

name: workflow
description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

name: working_directory
description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

name: write
description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
